feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-heavy roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive, light on quantified outcomes beyond scale metrics, and has a few style/grammar inconsistencies.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within one organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Strong strategic/technical blend: combines digital strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, governance, and multimedia in a way that feels senior and practical.  
- Good clarity and structure: headline, summary, competencies, experience, and technical skills are easy to scan and relevant to target roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more impact/results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include measurable improvements such as engagement growth, conversion gains, efficiency savings, adoption rates, or campaign performance.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these sections would tighten the CV and improve focus.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); “cross-channel” vs “Multi-channel” is inconsistent; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “A2 (learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and scope, but it reads a bit generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it around public-sector/advocacy digital leadership and platform transformation would make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with your niche: public-sector, advocacy, and mission-driven digital communications.
- Add one concrete differentiator such as enterprise web modernization, editorial systems, or cross-functional leadership.
- Trim broad lists of channels to avoid sounding repetitive.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading web, email, social, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, enterprise web modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics systems that support complex teams. Strong track record in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” closely echo Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, sharper terms and favor leadership-level phrasing:  
  Digital strategy & platform transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web operations & CMS administration • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder alignment & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy, policy & public-sector messaging • Multimedia, video & live event production
- Change “Multi-channel communication” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” for stronger grammar and seniority.
- Replace “Workflow & systems architecture” with “Workflow architecture & process improvement” unless you want to imply technical systems design specifically.
- Consider ordering by relevance to target roles: strategy, web/platforms, editorial/governance, analytics, stakeholder leadership, advocacy, multimedia.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This block substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider trimming either this section or the Topline Skills section.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and 2–3 signature contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact and scope: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancement, and communications operations for member-facing web properties.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 sharper points, e.g.:
- “Redesigned digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve cross-channel communications operations.”
- “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.”
- “Provided front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for high-visibility public web properties.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages, users, teams supported, launch dates, efficiency gains, engagement lifts.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; emphasize advisory/consulting impact here instead.
- Specific projects like AI search and microsites also appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating identical detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper, results-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add % improvements for traffic, publishing speed, engagement, production cost/time savings, reporting adoption, or decision-making cadence.
- Tighten channel language: replace “including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands…” with a more strategic outcome such as audience growth, engagement lift, or campaign impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this role focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, analytics, and governance.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with older multimedia bullets; frame it here as scaling in-house production capacity and organizational capability.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good channel breadth, but the item reads generic and overlaps with the more senior Director role. Tighten it around execution, team coordination, and channel growth, with clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership and scope: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy reach.”
- Combine and sharpen bullets: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-focused: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Clarify operational impact: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes and standardized publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Helping scale,” “helped improve,” and “strengthened” are vague; use direct verbs and outcomes.
- Avoid repeating governance/workflow language too closely with the Director of Digital Media entry unless this role shows the earlier build-out stage.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should be tightened to emphasize higher-level leadership strengths and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad terms with sharper, executive-level language: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise digital strategy and modernization”
- Make the list more distinctive and outcome-oriented where possible:
- Enterprise digital strategy and modernization
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this category to scale already proven in experience (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) rather than repeating generic skill labels.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” duplicates “Digital governance & editorial systems” in Core Competencies.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is very close to “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills area, emphasize platform leadership and modernization outcomes over individual technologies.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS leadership,” “CMS modernization and migration,” “Front-end implementation,” “API and workflow integration,” “AI-enabled search.”
- Cut lower-priority or older-signal items here (e.g., jQuery, Airtable systems) unless central to target roles; keep detailed tools in Technical + IT.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint and Power Pages • Enterprise CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • AI-enabled search and content experiences”
- If space allows, add scale language tied to recent work: “Enterprise CMS modernization for 10,000+ pages and 50+ publishers”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep this section higher-level and let Technical + IT hold the full stack/tool inventory.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; use one phrasing consistently.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making impact, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g. “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI & Looker Studio reporting” instead of listing tools separately.
- Replace generic phrases with sharper business language: “KPI framework design,” “executive dashboarding,” “behavior analysis with Microsoft Clarity,” “SEO and site performance optimization.”
- Consider this rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI & Looker Studio reporting • Microsoft Clarity behavior analysis • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO and web performance optimization”
- If space allows elsewhere, add one measurable proof point tied to recent NACo work (e.g. analytics stack supporting a 10,000+ page site and 3.5M annual page views).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.
- It also overlaps with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep this version strategic and let Technical + IT hold the fuller tool list.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize operational leadership and production capability rather than listing basic tasks/tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for scope and seniority: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows • Virtual event production”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more outcomes-oriented phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match the studio build and advocacy programming in recent roles.

- This item overlaps with Core Competencies (“Multimedia production and livestream operations”); use one for strategic framing and this one for execution specifics.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add proficiency/context or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling depth: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for impact: **Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- If Drupal is your clear lead platform, make that explicit: **Drupal-led CMS stack: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Keep punctuation consistent with other technical lists; avoid over-formatting or repeating implementation details covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one or using this version only for platform names while the other covers capabilities.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor versus enterprise platforms unless supported by project context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic coding terms.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping “HTML5”/“CSS3” in favor of “HTML/CSS” unless versioning matters; it feels dated.
- If accurate, add scope or outcomes in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., GTM used for analytics/event tracking, Workers for performance or routing, GitHub Actions for deployment automation.
- Order by strategic relevance: JavaScript/API integrations/GTM/Cloudflare Workers/GitHub Actions, then HTML/CSS/jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may also overlap with analytics infrastructure elsewhere; keep it here only if framed as implementation, not reporting.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since recent roles emphasize governance, automation, and cross-team operations, tighten this to highlight systems you actually used to build/coordinate workflows.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strategic relevance and likely recency: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light qualifiers instead of a bare list, e.g.: **Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate/Zapier (process automation) • Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp (project tracking) • Slack/Teams (cross-team coordination)**
- If space allows, replace 1–2 lower-value tools with scope language: **Built cross-department workflows and automations supporting editorial planning, approvals, and communications operations**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep them only if they support a systems/operations narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful tools to include, but this line is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal level of ownership. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and platform-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope/usage context instead of just listing tools, e.g. **Enterprise email automation, newsletter distribution, audience segmentation**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, lead with that platform first to reflect recency and depth

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating outcomes already covered in Work Experience (e.g., “newsletters reaching tens of thousands”).
- “Engagement” may overlap with broader digital strategy claims elsewhere; keep this item strictly tool/platform-oriented.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful “first in-house digital team” context, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-career buildout work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, audience growth, or production turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the management point: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” only if that support was meaningful and sustained.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, standardizing workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while mentoring a junior digital media colleague.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching/producing the series rather than expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; specify foundational setup here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generic and underplays impact. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/research support and the “first podcast” achievement.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout result: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research, project coordination, and digital content development.”
- Make the podcast line sharper and more outcome-oriented: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Trim vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; specify formats if possible (web articles, videos, graphics, member resources).
- Add any measurable scope if available: number of projects supported, episodes produced, stakeholders served, or programs/policy teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing general multimedia production; later roles already establish video/digital leadership more strongly.
- Don’t repeat broad web/email/social responsibilities here unless they were meaningfully distinct in this role.
